NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 899 5238 9466, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 899 5238 9466, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  POLICY DEVELOPMENT/ STRATEGIC PLANNING
  SESSION
  MARCH 9, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 3:04 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler
  Community Services Supervisor, Cynthia Morquecho
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  NONE

A.  PRESENTATION BY AVENU INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead introduced the item.

  Laura Burnett and Fran Mancia of Avenu Insights & Analytics, provided an update on
  present property tax trends, sales tax outlook in the City, review of the business
  license administration, and an update of the on-going business license discovery
  process.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED THIS ITEM RECEIVED AND FILED.

B.  PRESENTATION BY KATHLEEN MCGOWAN
  ENVIRONMENTAL/STORMWATER CONSULTANT

  Ms. McGowan, provided a Stormwater Program Update with the use of a Power Point
  presentation. Items included the Safe Clean Water Program, the Peninsula
  Watershed Management Group joint activities, upcoming items for City Council
  consideration, stormwater regulatory issues, and manure management as a
  resource.

  Discussion ensued amongst Council regarding anaerobic digesters as an
  environmentally and economically friendly waste management program.

  City Manager Grammer noted that this is a very preliminary idea and staff could seek
  out grant opportunities if the Council so directed.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 9, 2021
   Public Comment:

  Jonathan Cain spoke regarding the sustainability element benefits of anaerobic
  digesters; he encouraged seeking grant opportunities and encouraged such a
  program.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted consensus amongst Council for such an idea and
  directed staff to pursue the program.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED THIS ITEM RECEIVED AND FILED.

5.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  MID YEAR STATUS REPORTS
  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

City Manager Greg Grammer introduced the item noting the attached reports were provided
from each department regarding the status of activities at mid-year (FY 2020-21). He
included that it would be in order for the City Council to review, ask questions or provide
comments on any of the topics and receive and file the reports.

Administration report provided by Assistant City Manager Davis (as per the agenda
material).

Administrative Services report provided by Director Whitehead (as per the agenda
material).

Community Development and Public Works report provided by Director Wahba (as per the
agenda material).

Community Services report provided by Assistant City Manager Davis (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, THAT
THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE MID YEAR REPORTS.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT / STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION ITEMS
  Recommendation: That the City Council to consider the items presented and prioritize
  them on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

City Manager Greg Grammer introduced the item noting that City Council will be presented a
series of reports from respective departments detailing items for discussion.

City Manager Grammer requested to hear the Administration Outdoor Smoking Ban item
prior to Council taking a recess in order to accommodate those members of the public
wishing to speak on this item.

  ADMINISTRATION

  Outdoor Smoking Ban
  Council directed staff to return with a proposed draft ordinance.

  Public Comment:

  Alix Helena Politanoff, Project Coordinator of Behavioral Health Services, Inc. spoke
  regarding her work with local high schools on anti-vape and smoke free initiatives.

  Ryan Paillet Kick Ash Coalition Secretary spoke regarding public health and outdoor
  smoking ordinances in LA County.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 9, 2021
   Kelsie Groenleer, Kick Ash Coalition Member and Senior High student at Palos
  Verdes Peninsula High School, spoke regarding the organization’s efforts to promote
  a tobacco and smoke free environment through education on the dangers of second
  hand smoke.

  Council recessed at 5:10 p.m. and re-convened at 5:30 p.m. with all members present.

  Peninsula Cities Joint Lobbyist
  No Council action taken.

  Solid Waste/Recycling Updates
  Council Consensus to agendize in April 2021 Rate and service amendment with
  Waste Management.

  Diversity and Inclusion Policy
  Council Consensus to appoint Council Member Stegura & Council Member
  Schmitz to a subcommittee on development of the policy.

  Public Outreach and Engagement
  Council directed staff to agendize and return with additional information on the
  GoGov app

  Economic Development

  Economic Development Brochure
  No Council action required, informational only.

  CGI Banner Program
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Animal Control and Management

  Coyote Management Program
  No Council action taken.

  Peafowl Management
  No Council action taken.

  Gopher Remediation
  Council Consensus to proceed with the program and budget accordingly.

  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  Mid-Year Budget Review included:
  Fiscal Health Report, FY 2010-11 through FY 2019-20
  Finance Update
  Information Technology Update
  Fund Balance Policy Analysis General Fund Only

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED THIS ITEM RECEIVED AND FILED.

  FISCAL HEALTH REPORT

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a report.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED THIS ITEM RECEIVED AND FILED.

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT & PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  Standing-seam Metal Roofing Update
  Council directed staff to work with the Planning Commission to develop
  standards.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 9, 2021
   Preview of Upcoming 2021 Housing Legislation
  Council encouraged staff to monitor and bring any proposed bills that are of
  concern to the Council at the earliest possible time so they may engage in
  communications with local legislators.

  Review Restricting On-Street/overnight Parking Permits for New Accessory Dwelling
  Units (ADU) that are Located Within1/2 mile of a Transit Stop.
  Council Directed staff to explore the development of a parking permit program
  that includes neighborhood-specific parking permits, and to revisit the fee
  structure.

  Street Re-surfacing & Sidewalk Repair Projects
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Dapplegray School and PVDN Intersection Improvements
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Rolling Hills Road Improvements Storm Drain Repair Program
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Storm Drain Repair Program
  Council directed staff to address this issue in the coming fiscal year.

  Nationwide Street Sweeping Contract
  Council directed staff to bring back a renewal contract with Nationwide.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES

  Tree Trimming
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Peter Weber Equestrian Center Contract Renewal
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Community Garden
  Council directed staff to work with the Park and Activities Commission and
  agendize for future Council consideration.

  E-Bikes
  Council Consensus to review Municipal Code to consider Banning Off Street Use

  Community Services Project Updates
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Nature Center Project
  Council directed staff to utilize park facilities fees and continue seeking grant
  opportunities.

  City’s Plaque Policy
  Council approved establishing an equestrian recognition wall. No further Council
  action taken.

  Council discussion ensued over City plaque policy, assessment, and approval process.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, to not review or reconsider the plaque recognition policy as it exists.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None
  Motion carries

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 9, 2021
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, to put
  approval of the Armenian Genocide Memorial on a future agenda for reconsideration.

  AYES:  Huff, Zuckerman
  NOES:  Stegura, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion fails.

  Pepper Tree Foundation

  FY Determination
  No Council action required, informational only.

  Establishment of Fundraising Committee
  Council directed staff to return with a Fundraising Committee scope of
  work.

  Behested Payments
  Council directed staff to return with a policy.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 10:14 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the 7:00 pm
Regular City Council meeting via teleconference on March 23, 2021.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
Interim City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 9, 2021
